public_rationale: The records support substantial reported cash burn, particularly OpenAI's approximately $8 billion of negative free cash flow in 2025. They do not settle the stronger claim that neither company has a viable route to sustainability. Reported breakeven targets are relevant counterevidence to the absence of plans, but targets alone do not establish an achievable business model.
limitations: No objective probability threshold defines a real path.
The March Rothschild report provides no exact publication day; available_at uses month-end conservatively.
The cash-burn evidence is reported or estimated rather than a matched set of audited free-cash-flow statements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI are burning money and have no real path to financial sustainability.

statement.excerpt: Otherwise, you have to reconcile with the fact that both Anthropic and OpenAI are both incinerating money and have no real path to any kind of sustainability other than, well, not doing that.

from_speaker: no real path to any kind of sustainability
our_interpretation: Read incinerating money as substantial negative free cash flow, rather than treating financing proceeds or accounting losses as cash expenditure.
Read sustainability as the ability to cover ongoing business costs from customers without repeated external funding.
Use calendar 2025 for the cash-burn component, following the surrounding annual financial discussion.
Assess the asserted absence of a viable path as a present assessment at publication, not as a forecast with an invented deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Both companies have substantial cash burn, and evidence establishes that their documented operating plans cannot plausibly produce self-funding businesses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One company is already sustainably self-funding in the relevant period, or documented and sufficiently substantiated economics establish a viable route to that state.
